name: Cato Networks
short_description: Converges SD-WAN and security into a single secure access service edge.
why_relevant: The company that invented SASE and now serves thousands of enterprises.
history: Founded in 2015 by industry veterans Shlomo Kramer and Gur Shatz, Cato Networks pioneered the secure access service edge (SASE) category with its converged SD-WAN and security platform. It closed major funding rounds and reached a multi-billion-dollar valuation as enterprises adopted its single-vendor approach, expanding its global private backbone across hundreds of points of presence. The company added cloud-native security features such as secure web gateway and CASB. Today Cato serves thousands of organizations worldwide and is consistently recognized as a leader in SASE and network security.

name: SentinelOne
short_description: Autonomous endpoint protection that detects and responds to threats itself.
why_relevant: The AI-native EDR that challenges legacy signature-based vendors.
history: SentinelOne was founded in 2013 by Tomer Weingarten and Almog Cohen with a vision of autonomous, AI-driven endpoint defense. Its Singularity platform introduced patented behavioral AI that detects and responds to threats without human intervention, displacing signature-based tools. The company went public on the New York Stock Exchange in June 2021 and later expanded into identity, cloud and data security through acquisitions including Attivo Networks and PingSafe. With revenue growing past half a billion dollars and its Purple AI assistant, SentinelOne remains a leading challenger to legacy endpoint vendors.

name: CrowdStrike
short_description: Falcon platform for endpoint and identity protection in the cloud.
why_relevant: Defined the modern cloud endpoint security category at scale.
history: Founded in 2011 by George Kurtz, Dmitri Alperovitch and Gregg Marston, CrowdStrike launched the cloud-native Falcon platform in 2013, helping define the modern EDR category. It gained global prominence investigating the 2016 Democratic National Committee breach and went public in June 2019. Falcon unifies endpoint, identity, cloud and threat intelligence through a single lightweight agent, powering annual revenue beyond three billion dollars. After a widely documented update incident in 2024, the company reinforced its quality controls and retains a commanding position as the leading enterprise endpoint security platform.

name: Snyk
short_description: Developer-first security scanning for open-source dependencies and code.
why_relevant: Made secure-by-design development a default workflow for teams.
history: Snyk was founded in 2015 by Guy Podjarny, Danny Grander and Assaf Hefetz to put developer-first security directly into workflows. The company built a leading suite spanning open-source dependency scanning, static analysis, container security and SBOM management, and became one of Europe's highest-valued security startups after reaching a $4.7 billion round in 2021. Although valuations reset during the market downturn, Snyk continues to serve millions of developers and thousands of teams worldwide. Its tools remain instrumental in shifting application security left and embedding vulnerability remediation into everyday development practices.

name: Rubrik
short_description: Zero-trust data protection including immutability and cyber recovery.
why_relevant: The data-resilience layer behind many public ransomware-recovery returns.
history: Rubrik was founded in 2013 by Bipul Sinha, Arvind Jain, Soham Mazumdar and Aron Gibson to modernize backup and data management for the cloud era. The company scaled to a multi-billion-dollar valuation on the strength of its secure, immutable data storage, later acquiring Laminar to extend into data security posture management. In April 2024 Rubrik went public on the New York Stock Exchange, raising more than $750 million in its IPO. It now provides zero-trust data protection and cyber recovery to thousands of enterprise customers, positioning itself at the center of resilience against ransomware.

name: Cyera
short_description: Agentless data security that maps data and applies policies across clouds.
why_relevant: Fast-rising DSPM standard for knowing where sensitive data lives.
history: Founded in 2021 by Yotam Segev and Tamar Bar-Ilan, Cyera brought an agentless, AI-based approach to data security posture management. Its platform rapidly maps where sensitive data lives across cloud environments and automatically applies policy, striking a chord with teams contending with multi-cloud sprawl. The company raised a $300 million Series C in 2024, pushing its valuation past $1.4 billion, and acquired Trail Security to expand into data protection engines. Cyera now serves hundreds of enterprise customers discovering, classifying and governing sensitive data at scale, establishing itself as a DSPM standard-bearer.

name: Semperis
short_description: Protects and restores Active Directory and hybrid identity estates.
why_relevant: Multi-day AV recovery compressed to minutes for identity environments.
history: Semperis was founded in 2013 by Mickey Bresman to protect the identity systems most organizations depend on. Its Directory Services Protector delivers automated forest-wide recovery for Active Directory, compressing multi-day recovery efforts into minutes, complemented by the free Purple Knight security-assessment tool. The company achieved unicorn status with a $200 million Series C in 2022 and opened offices from New York to London. Serving Fortune 500 enterprises, government agencies and managed service providers, Semperis remains the recognized specialist for Active Directory and hybrid-identity resilience and recovery.

name: Armis
short_description: Senses and secures every connected and unmanaged device.
why_relevant: Massive IoT blind spot solved by passive network intelligence.
history: Armis was founded in 2015 by Yevgeny Dibner, Nadir Izrael and Tomer Schwartz to secure the exploding universe of connected and unmanaged devices. Its agentless, passive platform discovers and protects everything from IoT and OT systems to personal devices, closing a critical visibility gap for enterprises. The company reached unicorn status in 2019 and expanded into cloud and supply-chain environments while raising hundreds of millions in growth funding. Today Armis protects more than three billion assets worldwide and is a leading provider of unified asset intelligence and exposure management.

name: Orca Security
short_description: Agentless cloud security with a side-analyzer scan of cloud workload disks.
why_relevant: Asked no agents to secure every cloud workload in minutes.
history: Orca Security was founded in 2019 by Avi Shua, Gil Geron and Maty Siman to eliminate the operational burden of cloud security agents. Its patented side-scanning technology reads cloud workload disks out-of-band, delivering full CSPM, CWPP and CIEM coverage without installing any software. The company raised a $550 million Series C in 2021 and reached unicorn status, attracting customers across finance, healthcare and technology. Orca continues to expand its agentless platform with risk prioritization and threat detection, positioning itself as a leading approach to securing cloud workloads in minutes.

name: Aqua Security
short_description: Security for containers, serverless and the cloud-native application lifecycle.
why_relevant: Secured the Kubernetes wave before it became mainstream.
history: Aqua Security was founded in 2015 in Israel to secure the emerging cloud-native and container ecosystem. Its platform scans container images, hardens Kubernetes clusters and protects serverless workloads across the software lifecycle, backed by the discoveries of its Aqua Nautilus research team. The company raised more than $260 million, including a round that valued it at over $1 billion, and counts major enterprises among its customers. Aqua remains one of the most established names in container and cloud-native security.

name: Noname Security
short_description: Automated testing and posture management for APIs.
why_relevant: The API layer is now the primary attack path, and this is its watchdog.
history: Noname Security was founded in 2019 to protect the fast-growing API attack surface. Its platform combines automated testing, discovery and posture management to identify vulnerabilities across live and development APIs, gaining rapid adoption among enterprises and major cloud providers. In 2024 Akamai Technologies agreed to acquire the company, folding its API security technology into its platform. Noname's tools became a reference point for API security best practices, and its technology now helps secure millions of API transactions as part of a global security provider's portfolio.

name: Salt Security
short_description: AI-based platform protecting APIs from OWASP-API top-10 threats.
why_relevant: Hundreds of trillions of API calls analyzed to pre-empt abuse.
history: Salt Security was founded in 2016 by Roey Eliyahu and Michael Nicosia to defend APIs against increasingly sophisticated abuse. Its Pepper platform uses machine learning and traffic analysis to discover APIs and detect threats mapped to the OWASP API Top 10. The company closed a $140 million Series D in 2023 valuing it at $1.4 billion, with customers spanning banking, retail and technology. Salt continues to expand its API discovery, security testing and threat-intelligence capabilities, cementing its place among the leading dedicated API security providers.

name: Darktrace
short_description: Self-learning AI that detects novel attacks from network anomalies.
why_relevant: Grace-hopper-scale AI that starts secure with zero assumptions.
history: Darktrace was founded in 2013 by mathematicians and cybersecurity veterans from the University of Cambridge, pioneering an unsupervised, self-learning AI approach to network defense. The company listed on the London Stock Exchange in April 2021 and built a global footprint spanning email, cloud, OT and identity. Its anomaly-detection engine became known for spotting novel attacks without pre-written rules. In December 2024 private-equity firm Thoma Bravo agreed to acquire Darktrace for about $5.3 billion, taking the company private as it evolves toward an AI-first security platform.

name: Netskope
short_description: Cloud-delivered security for web, cloud apps and private apps.
why_relevant: The security cloud that moved enforcement to the edge of the internet.
history: Netskope was founded in 2012 by Sanjay Beri and experienced networking and security engineers to reimagine security for cloud-era traffic. Its private cloud network routes web, cloud and private application traffic through a global security fabric, moving enforcement to the internet edge. The company gained unicorn status in 2020 and expanded its portfolio with data protection, CASB, ZTNA and SASE offerings. Today Netskope protects enterprises from data loss and emerging threats across a worldwide network of points of presence and is recognized as a leader in SASE and cloud security.

name: Zscaler
short_description: Cloud-delivered zero trust access replacing legacy firewalled backbones.
why_relevant: The architecture blueprint of a password-and-VPN-free enterprise network.
history: Zscaler was founded in 2007 by Jay Chaudhry to deliver security and access from the cloud rather than from appliance-based backbones. Its Zero Trust Exchange replaced legacy VPNs and firewalls by connecting users to applications over brokered identity-driven sessions. Zscaler went public on Nasdaq in March 2018 and scaled to more than two billion dollars in annual revenue serving thousands of enterprises. The company continues to expand into AI-powered security, branch networking and OT, and remains the architectural reference for password-free, VPN-free zero trust access.

name: Chainguard
short_description: Builds minimal, repeatable, always-patched container images.
why_relevant: Every base image ships distroless and CVE-free by default.
history: Chainguard was founded in 2021 by Daniel Lorenc, Kim Lewandowski and others who built the open-source Sigstore software-signing project. The company set out to make supply-chain security practical by shipping minimal, distroless and continuously patched container images with embedded signing. It achieved unicorn status with a $61 million Series B in 2023 and partnered with major cloud providers and government agencies. Chainguard's approach gained traction amid hardening software-supply-chain requirements, making its CVE-free default base images a model for secure software development.

name: Island
short_description: Work browser that stops data leaving through the user's own browser.
why_relevant: Invented the enterprise browser category forcing a new device boundary.
history: Island was founded in 2018 by Mike Fey and Dan Amiga to invent the enterprise browser category. Its secure work browser enforces policy, controls data flow and integrates governance directly into the browsing layer, giving organizations a new enterprise-wide control point. The company emerged from stealth in 2022 and quickly reached a $3 billion valuation in 2023 through rapid revenue growth and enterprise adoption. Island's approach redefines the device boundary, enabling zero trust and data-loss prevention to be delivered where users actually work.

name: Abnormal Security
short_description: AI email security that detects business-email compromise style attacks.
why_relevant: Stopped executive impersonation attacks that spam filters miss.
history: Abnormal Security was founded in 2018 by Evan Reiser and Sanjay Jeyakumar to stop sophisticated email attacks using behavior-based AI rather than reputation scoring. Its platform models the identity and behavior of every user to detect business email compromise, vendor fraud and malicious links that traditional spam filters miss. The company scaled quickly, closing a $250 million round in 2024 at a $5.1 billion valuation. Abnormal now protects thousands of organizations worldwide and is a leading provider of AI-native email and identity security.

name: ArmorCode
short_description: Unifies security signals across code, cloud, APIs and containers.
why_relevant: One pane to prioritize the appsec findings that actually matter.
history: ArmorCode was founded in 2020 by Nikhil Gupta to unify a fragmented application security stack. Its ASPM platform aggregates findings from code, cloud, open-source, APIs and container tools into a single prioritized risk view, helping security and development teams act on what matters most. The company raised more than $40 million, including a Series B in 2023, and gained adoption among large enterprises managing dozens of security tools. ArmorCode continues to expand its application security posture management platform as the discipline becomes central to modern DevSecOps.

name: Astrix Security
short_description: Secures the explosion of machine and service identities in SaaS.
why_relevant: Tracks the automated identities attackers increasingly exploit.
history: Astrix Security was founded in 2021 by Alon Jackson and Idan Gour to address the explosive growth of non-human identities in modern software environments. Its platform discovers, classifies and continuously monitors machine and service identities, correlating their behavior to detect compromise and reduce associated risk. The company closed a $45 million Series A in 2023 led by prominent investors, winning customers across SaaS-heavy enterprises. Astrix continues to define the emerging non-human identity security category as attackers increasingly target automated credentials.

name: Torq
short_description: No-code security orchestration connecting every security tool.
why_relevant: Every security alert answered by a chain of automated responses.
history: Torq was founded in 2020 by Ofer Smadari and other security-industry veterans to bring no-code automation to security operations. Its hyperautomation platform connects dozens of security tools into visual workflows, letting analysts orchestrate responses without writing code. The company raised a $70 million Series B in 2023, attracted customers across fintech and retail, and gained recognition as a leader in security automation. Torq continues to expand its platform for building, running and sharing automated defense playbooks.

name: Varonis
short_description: Detects data exposure and insider risk inside cloud platforms.
why_relevant: Cleans the 'noise' inside files that make breaches so costly.
history: Varonis was founded in 2005 by Yaki Faitelson and Ohad Korkus to help organizations understand and protect their data. Its Metadata Framework automatically classifies files, folders and emails, detecting exposed sensitive data and insider-risk behavior across on-premises and cloud platforms. The company went public on Nasdaq in February 2014 and has grown into a global data security and governance leader. Varonis continually extends its platform with data classification, identity analytics and automated remediation, serving customers across heavily regulated industries.

name: KnowBe4
short_description: Simulates phishing and trains workforces into a human firewall.
why_relevant: Proved users can be the strongest line of defense when trained well.
history: KnowBe4 was founded in 2010 by Stu Sjouwerman to turn employees into a strong human line of defense. Its platform delivers simulated phishing attacks and security-awareness training at scale, training tens of thousands of organizations. The company went public in April 2021 and was later taken private by Vista Equity Partners in a deal valuing it at about $4.6 billion. KnowBe4 remains the dominant player in security awareness and human-risk management, continually expanding its training library and phishing simulations.

name: Cohesity
short_description: Simplifies backup onto one platform with AI-assisted recovery.
why_relevant: Combined data protection and security into one AI-native platform.
history: Cohesity was founded in 2013 by Mohit Aron to simplify secondary data storage with a single hyperconverged platform. Its DataProtect software consolidated fragmented backup environments and added AI-assisted recovery and ransomware defenses. In 2024 Cohesity announced plans to merge with Veritas to create a combined data-protection leader serving more than 12,000 customers. The company continues to deliver unified data management and cyber-resilience for enterprises worldwide.

name: Sysdig
short_description: Runtime security and compliance for containers and Kubernetes.
why_relevant: eBPF gives runtime evidence in real time without sidecars.
history: Sysdig was founded in 2013 by Loris Degioanni, creator of the Wireshark network analyzer, to bring deep visibility to containers and Kubernetes. The company open-sourced Falco, the runtime-security standard adopted by the CNCF, and pioneered eBPF-based runtime detection without requiring sidecars. Sysdig raised a $245 million Series E in 2022, surpassing a billion-dollar valuation, and expanded into cloud threat detection and compliance. Its platform remains a leading choice for cloud-native runtime security and remediation.

name: Devo
short_description: Security analytics cloud purpose-built for machine-speed log data.
why_relevant: Threat hunting at machine speed over petabyte-scale telemetry.
history: Devo was founded in 2011 to bring cloud-native speed to security analytics, combining fast data ingestion with a scale-out architecture. Its SIEM platform ingests machine-generated logs at machine speed, enabling threat hunting and investigation across petabyte-scale enterprise telemetry. The company raised more than half a billion dollars in funding, reaching a $2 billion valuation in 2021, and operates global R&D and go-to-market teams. Devo continues to serve security operations centers worldwide with its high-scale, event-driven analytics cloud.

name: Exabeam
short_description: Behavioral analytics that spot insider threats and account misuse.
why_relevant: Uses behavior baselines to flag the attacker, not just the flag.
history: Exabeam was founded in 2013 by Nir Polak and Sylvain Gil to make security teams dramatically more productive. Its New-Scale SIEM and behavioral analytics platform builds baselines of user and entity behavior to spot insider threats, account misuse and modern attacks. The company raised funding from investors including Lightspeed and Cisco and earned recognition as a leader in SIEM and UEBA. Exabeam continues to evolve its AI-driven approach to security investigations and detection engineering.

name: Sumo Logic
short_description: Cloud-native log analytics and SIEM for app and infra pipelines.
why_relevant: Its 'monitor everything' posture cuts incident mean-time-to-respond.
history: Sumo Logic was founded in 2010 by Christian Beedgen, Kumar Saurabh and Bruno Kurtic to deliver log intelligence as a cloud service. Its continuous-intelligence platform ingests application and infrastructure data at massive scale, supporting observability and cloud SIEM under one subscription. The company went public on Nasdaq in 2020 and was later taken private by Francisco Partners in a deal valued at about $1.7 billion. Sumo Logic continues to help enterprises monitor, secure and troubleshoot modern application pipelines from a single cloud-native platform.

name: Lookout
short_description: Secure mobile endpoint against malware, phishing and app risks.
why_relevant: Smartphones are the unstoppable device; Lookout watches them.
history: Lookout was founded in 2007 by John Hering, James Burgess and Kevin Mahaffey, pioneers of mobile security. Its cloud-based platform detects mobile malware, phishing and risky apps, protecting enterprise smartphones and providing mobile threat defense for government and critical infrastructure. The company raised substantial venture funding and reached a $1.9 billion valuation in 2019. Lookout continues to protect devices, users and critical infrastructure across enterprise and government sectors, expanding from mobile security into endpoint and identity.

name: Zimperium
short_description: On-device AI that detects mobile malware without sending data to cloud.
why_relevant: Mobile-only sandbox detections based on behavior preclude evasion.
history: Zimperium was founded in 2010 by Zuk Avraham and security researchers specializing in mobile platforms. Its on-device z9 engine detects malware and phishing locally using machine learning, without uploading data to the cloud. Zimperium's technology has protected critical public and private organizations and helped pioneer the mobile threat defense category. The company continues to expand its mobile security platform, focusing on comprehensive mobile threat defense for enterprises and government agencies.

name: Avanan
short_description: Cloud email security layer on top of Microsoft and Google.
why_relevant: Detects prompt-injection and AI-opened harmful links in mail.
history: Avanan was founded in 2015 by Gil Friedrich and Ohad Bobrov to layer AI-powered security on top of Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace. Its API-based cloud email security detects phishing, spoofing and, more recently, prompt-injection and AI-opened malicious links that native mail defenses miss. In 2021 Check Point Software acquired Avanan to create its Harmony Email and Collaboration solution. Avanan's technology now protects millions of mailboxes as an integral part of a global enterprise security portfolio.

name: Fireblocks
short_description: Custody and transfer infrastructure for institutional crypto.
why_relevant: The safe rails banks use to hold and move digital assets.
history: Fireblocks was founded in 2018 by Michael Shaulov, Pavel Berengoltz and Idan Ofrat to secure institutional digital-asset operations. Its platform uses multi-party computation (MPC) and hardware isolation to custody and transfer crypto assets, becoming the trusted rail for exchanges, banks and funds. The company quickly scaled to serve hundreds of institutions, raising $550 million in 2022 at an $8 billion valuation. Fireblocks continues to expand its network and its wallet, tokenization and policy-control capabilities for the regulated digital-asset economy.
